questions.stem: If a business buys a car for ₦500,000 on credit, what happens to the accounting equation?
questions.explanation: When a car is purchased on credit, both assets (the car) and liabilities (the credit) increase by the same amount, keeping the equation balanced.

distractorRationale.a: Assets increase, but liabilities also increase, not decrease.
distractorRationale.b: Assets do not decrease; they increase.
distractorRationale.d: Both assets and liabilities change in this transaction.

questions.stem: Which of the following is classified as an asset?
questions.explanation: Office furniture is a resource owned by the business, thus classified as an asset.

distractorRationale.a: Bank loan is a liability, not an asset.
distractorRationale.c: Accounts payable is a liability, not an asset.
distractorRationale.d: Owner's equity is capital, not an asset.
